newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower after CPI release.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower after CPI release.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed lower on Sunday following the release on Friday of October's consumer price index (CPI), traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.77 percent, or 1.5 points, to 193.87 on a low all-share turnover of 43 million shekels against 71 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.86 percent to 203.14.
The CPI rose 0.8 percent in October against a rise of 0.4 percent in September.

"The CPI was within expectations but for some reason investors were hoping for a lower figure. The Bank of Israel might leave the interest rate unchanged or lower it by only 0.25-0.3 percentage point," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"Activity continues to be low, but despite that the market posted nice gains during the last two weeks," Nahum said.
Makhteshim Chemical Works fell 2.75 percent to 1,940 after reporting a decline in third-quarter net profit to $2.6 million from $3.5 million a year earlier.
Delek the Israel Fuel Corp DELK.TA fell 1.0 percent to 7,384 after reporting third-quarter net profit of 26.64 million shekels against 25.15 million shekels a year earlier.

Elron Electronic Industries closed unchanged at 11,777 after Lehman Brothers lowered its 1996 earnings estimate for the company to $0.50 per share from $0.62. Despite that Lehman is holding to its 1997 forecast of $0.72.
Tadiran fell 3.0 percent to 1,454 after its issue traded in New York fell 2.8 percent on Thursday and Friday.

"Activity was very low today and investors showed no interest in trading. The CPI was within expectations and it's hard to believe that the central bank will lower interest rates," said Elish Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.5 percent to 28,740 on volume of 1.7 million shekels; Elbit, which rose 1.75 percent to 13,485 on turnover of 1.5 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which fell 0.75 percent to 384 on volume of 1.4 million shekels.
Africa Israel Hotels fell 5.0 percent to 294 following a sharp rise of more than 14 percent last week.
